fee.title: UGA Admissions - Application fee and fee waivers

aid.title: UGA Student Financial Aid - Academic scholarships

test_policy.notes: Official SAT or ACT scores are required of all first-year applicants; there is no test-optional pathway. UGA superscores both tests. Minimums set by the Board of Regents: SAT EBRW 480 and Math 440, or ACT English or Reading 17 and Math 17.

requirements.notes: First-year application fee is $70 for US citizens and $85 for international students. Letters of recommendation are optional (one is highly recommended). International students should choose 'Do not self-report grades' and send final English-translated transcripts; UGA recalculates the GPA.

deadlines.label: Early action (non-binding)
deadlines.notes: Materials deadline Oct 29. Decisions for non-Georgia residents in mid-December; most EA applicants are deferred to the regular timeline.

deadlines.label: Regular decision
deadlines.notes: Materials deadline Jan 15; final decisions in mid-March.

deadlines.label: Foundation Fellowship application
deadlines.notes: Separate application; open to international first-years.

english_policy.waiver_notes: No separate English test is required of first-year applicants: SAT or ACT scores, which every applicant must submit, are used as proof of English proficiency. TOEFL or IELTS may also be submitted. Average scores of admitted international students (2019-2023) were SAT EBRW 650, ACT English 30, IELTS 7.5, TOEFL 102 (5.0 on the new scale); these are averages, not minimums.

aid.notes: The Foundation Fellowship (application due Nov 1) is open to international first-years: $30,000 stipend plus a waiver of the difference between in-state and international tuition. The need-and-merit scholarships listed require Georgia residency and a FAFSA.

tier_notes.engineering: College of Engineering is young (2012) and not yet highly ranked.
